chapter: Minton's, bop and the Monk circle
title: How ideas come, dry spells and why she won't be a hired arranger
summary: Ideas come from nowhere or from the subway wheels; she runs dry and will not take a job as arranger. She creates best playing with a bass player.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Even when you were writing new things, did you sometimes reach into your own past to get ideas?

No. I tell you what it happensa. It would just come right out. You may be walking down the street and it comes out of the sky. But there's other times when you don't feel like writing or you're just dry. I would never take a job as an arranger or creative artist because you can run dry and you just have to leave it alone for 6 months, 4 to 6 months. Sometimes riding on the subway would inspire me, the clicking of the wheels, to write something. But there are times when everything is completely gone as if you've never written anything and nothing happens at all.
A dry spell. You say you wouldn't take a job as a creative artist, what are you doing - ?
I mean as an arranger or writer, that's what I mean, because I'm too creative. I have to wait for an inspiration.
But every time you sit down to play you've been creative.
Yes, it's better for me that way. I can create much better if the bass player's with me, if he doesn't interfere.
Now, want to stop a minute?
